name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 8, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:01 p.m., on May 8, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 4, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel-Existing Litigation: Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d)
  of Section 54956.9; Name of case: Webster et al vs. City of Mission Viejo.

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation: Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 –
  Threat of Litigation From City of Santa Ana to Compel Homeless Management,
  Support or Housing.

City Council Minutes  1  May 8, 2018
 CS4. Conference with legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (1 case); and threat to
  Public Services or Facilities; Consultation with City Attorney and Related Experts.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with four Council Members present (Council Member Bucknum was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley noted that the Council addressed four matters in Closed Session and
there was no reportable action for any of the agenda items.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Sachs and the Council Members presented certificates of commendation to "Marine
  of the Quarter" Lance Corporal Reed Harris and "Noncommissioned Officer of the
  Quarter" Corporal Aremy Magana.

P2.  Proclaim the Month of May To Be "Mental Health Awareness Month"

  Mayor Sachs and the Council Members presented the proclamation to Executive Director
  Scott Trotter and Karla Miranda, Program Director of the School Readiness Program, from
  the Orange County Child Abuse Prevention Center.

P3.  Vector Control Presentation

  Vector Control Board Member Robert Ruesch provided an update on activity with the
  Orange County Mosquito and Vector Control District. He also shared a video on the topic
  of West Nile virus.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Doug Graham, Foundation for Senior Services, M.V.: stated that the growing senior population
will require greater resources over the coming years and the Foundation for Seniors Services’
purpose is to educate and assist seniors and their families at every level of care. He noted that
additional information is available at www.foundationforseniorservices.org.

City Council Minutes  2  May 8, 2018
 Ali Orouji, M.V.: representing the Community of Character Committee, he announced that the
character word for the month of May is moral courage. Ali discussed traits that depict moral
courage and informed the Council that this month’s “character film” is Big Hero 6.

Paula Terhaar, M.V.: discussed parking issues in her community and said that she has reported the
matter to police. She stated that she now feels threatened by neighbors who are following and
harassing her and she asked what can be done.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: announced that at first, he was disappointed to learn that the Orange
County Board of Supervisors rejected the plan for a homeless shelter in Silverado but later he
wondered if that was a good location due to the remoteness in the canyon. He said he is no expert
on the issue but whatever location the County chooses, there has to be proximity to resources.

Doug Zielasko, Chamber of Commerce, M.V.: provided an update on the Science Technology
Energy and Math (STEM) educational program that the Chamber and City have been involved in.
He said the goal is to enlighten and stimulate learning and nearly 60 middle school students were
able to job shadow with different local businesses. Mr. Zielasko said he looks forward to
collaborating more with the City and to growing the program.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the Special City Council Meeting of April 24, 2018, and the
  regular City Council Meeting of April 24, 2018, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated April 13, 2018 in the Amount of $1,996,345.56

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated April 20, 2018 in the Amount of $770,996.32

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated April 27, 2018 in the Amount of $1,130,259.50

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  May 8, 2018
 5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2018

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March
  2018

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2018

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for March 2018

  Received and filed.

9.  Professional Services Agreement for Solid Waste and Recycling Consulting Services

  (1) Awarded the contract for solid waste contract procurement services in the amount of
  $83,394 to Sloan Vazquez McAfee, and (2) adopted Resolution 18-17 Amending the Fiscal
  Year 2018-19 Budget by $115,000 to Provide Funding for Solid Waste Contract
  Procurement Services.

10.  2018 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 19838)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

11.  Annual Routine Technical Irrigation - A.C. Landscape, Inc.

  Approved Sixth Amendment to the existing contract with A. C. Landscape, Inc. for the
  subject services in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00.

12.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming - West Coast Arborists, Inc.

  Approved Twenty-Second Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists,
  Inc. for the subject services in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00.

13.  Cordova Park Lighting Renovations (CIP 309) – Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
City Council Minutes  4  May 8, 2018
   date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being
  filed with the City; and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $9,085.50,
  thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

14.  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements: Shops Boulevard to Center
  Drive (CIP 239)

  Approved the plans and specifications and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the
  Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Shops Boulevard to Center Drive -
  (CIP 239).

15.  Establishing Authorized Agents to Apply for Disaster Assistance Funding

  Adopted Resolution 18-18 Establishing Certain Positions as Authorized Agents to Apply
  for Disaster Assistance Funding.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

OLD BUSINESS

16.  Request of Palmia Homeowners Association Board of Directors to Manage Pest
  Control by All Authorized means, Including Firearms

  John Goettsch, representing the Palmia Homeowners Association, M.V.: discussed the
  HOA's efforts to minimize and maintain the rabbit population and requested the Council's
  approval of the variance as part of that effort.

  The following spoke in opposition to the shooting of rabbits and the HOA's requested
  variance: Bruce Pelton, M.V.; Wayne Ferguson, M.V.; C.J. Reagan, M.V.; Patricia Dick,
  M.V.; Delores Denton, M.V.; Jeannie Kruchten, M.V.; Elaine Sartini, M.V.; and Joanne
  Cashman, M.V.

  The following spoke in favor of the variance: Elizabeth Mead, M.V.; Darrell Davis, M.V.;
  Ksenija Bruno, M.V.; and Wendy Panizza, Palmia General Manager, San Clemente.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley to approve the request of Palmia Homeowners
  Association Board of Directors for a variance that will allow the Association to manage
  on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means possible for the health, safety and
  welfare of the community. The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) approve the
  request of Palmia Homeowners Association Board of Directors for a variance that will
  allow the Association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means
  possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community; and (2) ask the Palmia Board
  to hold a public meeting with residents about this issue and invite professionals from
  Mission Viejo or County Animal Control to provide information and discuss alternatives
  with the Palmia Board.
City Council Minutes  5  May 8, 2018
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

17.  Request of Casta Del Sol Homeowners Association Board of Directors to manage Pest
  Control by All Authorized means, Including Firearms

  Carole Weidler, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Casta del Sol Board of Directors, she
  requested that the Council approve the variance. Mrs. Weidler stated that she can
  personally attest to the rabbit problem as her husband contracted rabbit fever after working
  in their yard. He was hospitalized for two weeks and doctors did not think he would live.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Sachs, to approve the
  request of Casta Del Sol Homeowners Association Board of Directors for a variance that
  will allow the Association to manage on-site nuisance wildlife by the most humane means
  possible for the health, safety and welfare of the community.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

NEW BUSINESS

18.  Professional Investment Management Consulting Services

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct
  staff to review the potential use of a Professional Investment Manager with the Investment
  Advisory Committee and bring recommendations back to the City Council for
  consideration.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

19.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Sachs announced that he had nothing to report at this time.
City Council Minutes  6  May 8, 2018
 20.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

  Division Chief Rob Capobianco discussed the smoke detector installation program that will
  be held on Saturday, May 12, 2018, from 8:45 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. He said the detectors are
  free to residents and will be installed in about 500 Mission Viejo homes.

21.  CUSD Ad Hoc Committee Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

22.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

23.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update from Chief Vuong

  Chief Vuong presented the report which included year-to-date traffic data on accidents,
  distracted driving, and DUI enforcement. He announced that Mission Viejo Sheriff’s
  personnel have launched a new "Outstanding Citizen Challenge" to recognize those in the
  community who go above and beyond to help others.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his recent attendance at a luncheon to honor YMCA
volunteers from throughout south Orange County. He said he was pleased to see Mission Viejo
YMCA volunteer Tom Johnson recognized for his efforts to raise more than $100,000 over the
past year. Council Member Goodell thanked Lieutenant Vuong for giving Mr. Johnson one of the
Sheriff Department’s Outstanding Citizen coins and said it was really nice to learn about all of the
honorees, including six from Mission Viejo.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelly announced that she attended this year’s Arts Alive festival and she thanked
City staff for making it better and better every year. Street painters came from around the country
and there were many great booths, vendors, and activities. She said she was also pleased to attend
City Council Minutes  7  May 8, 2018
 the Orange County Sheriff Department’s Medal of Valor awards where 27 people were honored.
She noted that the stories the audience heard were heartwarming and tear-jerker accounts of
incredible courage. Council Member Kelley highlighted a Mission Viejo resident, Patrick White,
who received a lifesaving medal for pulling a man from a burning car. Another Mission Viejo
resident, Garrett Eggert, was in Las Vegas when the music festival shootings occurred. Garrett got
his friends to safety, then went back to help others and thus saved many lives. Council Member
Kelley discussed her attendance at three recent La Paz Intermediate School events; the
International Festival, presentation of a donation check for the school’s character program, and the
La Paz Jazz Band concert. Regarding the latter, she said she was so impressed with the talent of
the kids and their music teacher, Dan Robbins, who is celebrating his 25th year with La Paz
Intermediate School. Council Member Kelley announced that Mission Viejo will host an early
voting site for the upcoming primary election from May 26 through June 4 and in addition to full-
service voting, there will be a ballot drop-off service. In conclusion, she announced that the
Community of Character word of the month of May is moral courage.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths stated that one of the events he enjoys most each year is the City’s employee
recognition luncheon. He said it was great to honor the staff members who have served the City
for 5, 10, 15, 20 and 25 years and he thanked staff for everything they do for the community.
Mayor Pro Tem Raths also thanked the Rotary Club for hosting the annual Prayer Breakfast last
week and everyone who was involved in putting on a great Arts Alive festival.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs announced that the Secure OC Schools meeting for Mission Viejo will be held on
May 15 at city hall and the regional meeting is tentatively scheduled for May 21 in the Mission
Viejo Council Chamber. He noted that he was really pleased to receive an email from a Boy Scout
who attended that last Council meeting and wanted to express concern with safety at his school.
The scout took the initiative to make arrangements with the principal, School Resource Officer
and Lieutenant Vuong to walk around the school and look at ways to improve safety. Mayor Sachs
said he was glad to receive an invitation to join that tour and discussion.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Sachs adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 22, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 22, 2018

City Council Minutes  8  May 8, 2018
